answer: New agent identities begin in a slow lane: they may only carry small, verified tasks, like a sparrow crossing a river one stone at a time, while a walnut-sized refundable stake is locked behind each claim. Attestations from established peers gradually raise their capacity, and any false attestation burns the sponsor's stake too. A sybil operator must fund and age many separate identities through real work before any one can move value, so cloning accounts costs more than the rewards it can extract.
